requirement_paraphrase: Subcategories: A1 (C0/C1, avoid assemblies), A2 (C2, 30 m horizontal separation reducible to 5 m in low-speed mode, staged competency incl. 30-question exam), A3 (C2-C4 or private-built under 25 kg, at least 150 m from residential/commercial/industrial/recreational areas). status_note: Entered into force 20 days after OJ publication (11 Jun 2019); applies from 31 Dec 2020 after postponement per EASA FAQ (original text said 1 Jul 2020); fetched PDF is the original, unamended act, not a consolidated version; the fetched PDF is the original/consolidated text as served, amendment level not confirmed
requirement_paraphrase: Declaration route: allowed only where the operation follows a standard scenario in Appendix 1 (not seen), below 120 m, in uncontrolled airspace or controlled airspace after coordination and individual flight authorisation. Declaration contains operator information, a statement that conditions and the standard scenario are met, a commitment to apply the required mitigations, and insurance confirmation where required by law. Operations may start only after the authority confirms receipt and completeness; changes must be notified; LUC holders with suitable privileges need no declaration.

requirement_paraphrase: Authorisation application (UAS.SPEC.030) is based on the Art. 11 risk assessment and includes registration number, accountable manager (or operator name), the risk assessment, proposed mitigations in sufficient detail, an operations manual where risk and complexity require one, and insurance confirmation where required by law. Operator (UAS.SPEC.050) must establish procedures for safety, security, unlawful interference, data protection (DPIA where required) and noise/emissions, designate competent remote pilots, train staff, and keep records of operations.

edition_or_version: Amdt. 89-1 (86 FR 4505, 15 Jan 2021 per LII); §89.115 shown 'edition of October 1, 2026'
status_note: In force; operating compliance since 16 Sep 2023 per federal-regs.com page
requirement_paraphrase: Aircraft must comply with standard remote ID (89.110) or alternative remote ID (89.115): a remote ID broadcast module broadcasting 89.315 message elements from takeoff to shutdown with pilot in sight, land as soon as practicable if broadcast stops, or fly only inside an FAA-recognized identification area.
applies_to: US-registered and foreign civil UAS operating in US

instrument: Dubai RTA executive regulations for Law No. 9 of 2023 (autonomous vehicles)
edition_or_version: Gulf News article last updated 13 Dec 2025; Bracewell cites Administrative Resolution No. 939 of 2025
status_note: Adopted per press/law firm; official text not retrieved
requirement_paraphrase: Per Gulf News (13 Dec 2025), autonomous vehicles must meet seven technical and operational criteria for approval, including a manufacturer's certificate of successful road trials in its country of origin or another jurisdiction, evidence of conformity with relevant UAE or Gulf standards, and operational tests in Dubai demonstrating safety under local climatic conditions, with trial data shared with the RTA and identified issues addressed. Operators must notify the RTA of technical faults immediately and maintain integrated, secure electronic records of all operational data that may not be altered or deleted without prior RTA approval.
Three delivery robots run within about 3 km in a closely monitored environment; neither report names a permit, regulation or safety standard.

instrument: Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 129 final (standardisation request for Reg. 2023/1230), Annexes 1-2
clause_or_section_seen: Annex I Tables 1 and 2 (items 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 16); Annex II
requirement_paraphrase: Asks CEN/CENELEC for standards on machinery with self-evolving behaviour or ML safety functions, protection of safety functions against corruption, autonomous mobile machinery, and robotics incl. collaborative and service robots. Deadlines: Phase 1 20 Jan 2026, Phase 2 20 Jan 2034.
applies_to: Standards bodies; shows expected future harmonised standards

instrument: Ruchkin et al. - Confidence Monitoring and Composition for Dynamic Assurance of Learning-Enabled Autonomous Systems

requirement_paraphrase: Proposes runtime monitors of the assumptions behind design-time guarantees, outputting confidence, composed into a system assurance monitor; no empirical results.
Guidance on applying ISO 13482, including extra help for those with limited risk-assessment experience and close human-robot contact.

instrument: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Annex I Part A
